champion: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated myeloid neoplasm
ordered_diagnoses: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated myeloid neoplasm

facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

concepts.why: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, and negative for myeloperoxidase, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The patient's history of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts supports this diagnosis.
The patient's history of refractory anemia with excess blasts and bone marrow biopsy showing 10% to 15% myeloblasts supports this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated myeloid neoplasm
concepts.why: The presence of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and myelodysplastic syndrome, with identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes, suggests a diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis with associated myeloid neoplasm.
The presence of BRAF-V600E variant status identified through immunohistochemical studies explains the uncovered finding of this specific mutation.

rationales.F05: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F06: Uniform positivity for CD207/langerin is a specific marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: The presence of a BRAF-V600E variant is commonly associated with Langerhans cell histiocytosis and other neoplastic conditions.
rationales.F10: The identification of identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in both bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens suggests a clonal relationship between the myeloid neoplasm and the Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
